cases.description: Five envelopes are accepted. A signs a void for position 3: it is appended as position 6, which becomes the head. The same record again is an exact retry: 200 with the original position. A pull then shows the five envelopes and the void by position.
cases.name: a_member_signed_void_is_appended_at_the_next_seq

cases.description: B's credential carries a void that A signed, and A's credential carries one that B signed: the signer need not be the credential's device.
cases.name: any_member_may_send_and_any_member_may_sign

cases.description: A and B each sign a void for position 3, and A signs a second, different one (another issued_at). All three are kept at positions 6, 7 and 8; none is deduped as a second void for the same seq. A replay of the envelope at 3 returns every claim in append order.
cases.name: two_distinct_claims_for_one_position_are_both_kept

cases.description: A void for position 2 is appended; replicas decide whether it is honored, so the server must still accept a void for position 4, which that void's range would cover if it were honored, and one for position 1.
cases.name: an_earlier_void_never_blocks_a_later_one

cases.description: C is not in the chain. C's void is VoidSignerNotAuthorized (403) whoever carries it, the head does not move, and a pull has no voids member.
cases.name: a_signer_who_is_not_a_member_is_refused

cases.description: One flipped signature bit is VoidSignatureInvalid (400).
cases.name: a_signature_that_does_not_verify_is_refused

cases.description: A void whose command id or envelope digest differs from the index's record, one for a position beyond the head, position 0, and one for a position a void occupies (not a command envelope) are VoidTargetMismatch (409).
cases.name: a_void_must_name_the_envelope_the_index_holds

cases.description: A truncated record, a protocol version other than 1 inside the body, and a void for another vault are MalformedObject (400); a suite other than 1 is UnsupportedSuite (400). Each is refused before its signer is looked at.
cases.name: a_record_that_cannot_be_parsed_is_refused

cases.description: The first failing step answers. A truncated record, a void for another vault and a suite other than 1 are answered even when writes are suspended (MalformedObject, UnsupportedSuite). An exact retry of an appended void is 200 even when writes are suspended; a new void then is WritesSuspended before its signer or its target is looked at; with writes allowed a non-member signer is answered before a mismatched target, a bad signature before a mismatched target, and a mismatched target before QuotaExceeded.
cases.name: the_decision_order_of_appendvoid

cases.description: Envelopes 1 and 2, a void at 3 (naming 2), envelopes 4 and 5, and an epoch entry at the head, then a void at 7 (naming 5). A full pull lists every position once: the epoch entry follows the log object whose seq is its position. The voids member is present only on pages that hold a void.
cases.name: voids_and_envelopes_share_one_sequence_in_pulls

cases.description: Envelopes 1 to 3 and a void at 4, in pages of three log objects. The second page has no envelope entry and carries the void with has_more false, so a client that stops on an empty entries list would lose it; the page before it says has_more true.
cases.name: a_page_can_hold_only_a_void

cases.description: A reports a stop at 3. A's stageSnapshot, publishSnapshot and installEpoch are then ReplicaHalted (409) with the reported position; B's pass the gate, an account credential passes (it has no device), and A can still append a void, report again (the latest report wins) and pull. A reports null and A's requests pass the gate again.
cases.name: a_halt_is_reported_refused_and_cleared

cases.description: B cannot report A's halt (Forbidden, 403) or clear it, and a refused report records nothing.
cases.name: a_device_reports_only_its_own_halt

decision_order_of_appendvoid: 1 authenticate (not exercised: every credential here is valid)
2 parse: MalformedObject (framing, body, a protocol version other than 1, another vault), UnsupportedSuite
3 exact retry: a void with this void_id is in the log: 200 with its position
5 signer: VoidSignerNotAuthorized, then VoidSignatureInvalid (the verify_void of sync-core)
how_to_read: Each case is a list of steps against ONE server that starts empty: a vault with the 'chain' below, head 0, no halts, writes permitted and no quota exceeded. A step may change those with 'conditions' (writes_permitted false, quota_exceeded true), for that step only. 'credential' names the device whose credential carries the request ('A', 'B', or 'account' for an account credential). 'pushEnvelope' stands for an accepted envelope: it appends an identity (command_id, envelope_digest) to the accepted-envelope index at head + 1, so cases need no sealed envelope. 'recordEpochEntry' stands for an installed epoch record at the current head (an epoch entry; it takes no seq). 'replayPush' is an exact replay of the envelope accepted at 'seq'. 'stageSnapshot', 'publishSnapshot' and 'installEpoch' stand for those requests arriving at the halt gate of section 4.12: the outcome is the gate's refusal, or {"gate": "pass"} when the request goes on to its own decision procedure. 'expect' is the outcome: a 'status' and the response members named, or 'error' for a non-2xx response, or 'details'. A pull's 'entries' lists the page's envelope and epoch entries as 'envelope:SEQ' and 'epoch:POSITION', and its 'voids' (absent when the page holds none) lists the voids by position and void id; a client merges them by seq. A 'void_id' is SHA-256 of the void body. In 'reportHalt', 'device' names the {device_id} in the path.
spec: docs/architecture/sync-service-protocol.md 4.11, 4.12 and 11.2; ADR 0074 Addendum D and E; docs/architecture/vault-format.md C.10 "Void records"
synthetic: Every value is synthetic. The chain, its keys and the signatures are made from fixed seeds that live only in the generator (crates/sync-core/tests/sync_service_void_vectors.rs); the file holds the signed records. Command ids and envelope digests are repeated bytes.
